title: A 0.29pJ/b 5.27Tb/s/mm UCIe Advanced Package Link in 3nm FinFET with 2.5D CoWoS Packaging
problem: Heterogeneous chiplet-based SiPs require high-bandwidth, low-power, low-latency die-to-die (D2D) links with reliable BER, but proprietary solutions limit vendor interoperability; standardization is needed.
motivation: Disaggregation of SoCs across multiple technology nodes in 2.5D packages demands efficient interconnects; UCIe standard enables cross-vendor interoperability and eliminates custom D2D design burden.
method: The team designed a standardized chip-to-chip data link following the UCIe standard (a universal format for connecting modular computer chips), capable of transferring 4 to 16 billion bits per second through each connection pin. They implemented this using 3nm FinFET transistors—extremely small, efficient transistors—and packaged the design using 2.5D CoWoS-S technology, which arranges and connects chips on a substrate. The result achieves 5.27 terabits per second of bandwidth density and consumes only 0.29 picojoules of energy per bit transmitted.
key_novelty: This work proves for the first time that standardized chip-to-chip links (UCIe) using 2.5D CoWoS packaging can match or exceed the efficiency and bandwidth of custom proprietary designs.
contributions: 4-to-16Gb/s/pin UCIe-compliant transceiver enabling standard-based chiplet interoperability
2.5D CoWoS-S package integration demonstrating practical heterogeneous SiP deployment
Low-latency, reliable BER performance for chiplet communication

metrics.other: 4-to-16 Gb/s/pin per UCIe spec, low BER

baselines: Proprietary D2D links (refs 2-7); prior chiplet solutions
limitations: Comparison with alternative packaging technologies and other standards not discussed; scalability beyond 3nm or 2.5D CoWoS-S not addressed.
